name: PlayStation 5 (disc edition)
summary: Sony's 2020 console. Two white side panels pop off without tools; the fan, SSD cover and disc drive come out from the right, and the power supply sits deeper under a shield plate. No battery: the power supply plays that role.

specs.Processor: AMD custom Zen 2, 8 cores / 16 threads, 3.5 GHz
specs.Cooling: 120 mm centrifugal fan, liquid-metal CPU interface

sources.title: iFixit: How to Upgrade the Expandable Storage in a PlayStation 5
MP1st: PS5 Weight, Dimensions and Box Art Revealed (secondary report of Sony's figures; playstation.com tech-specs URL returned 404)

verification.notes: Removal order, screws and tools come from iFixit's Fan, Power Supply and Storage guides and the Teardown (read 2026-11-09). Specs are from the teardown. Dimensions 390 x 260 x 104 mm (modelled lying down) are a secondary report of Sony's figures; playstation.com's tech-specs URL returned 404. No second independent teardown was read, so only one source family backs every part. The PS5 has no battery, so the power supply is modelled as the engine's power source; 'disconnect battery' means unplug the mains. TR8/TR9 Torx are not in the tool list, so tools are given in notes. Not modelled: Wi-Fi/antennas, front USB, LED and power button boards, the M.2 expansion SSD. Components with verified=false (mainboard, chassis-frame) need a check. Geometry is approximate. Failure behaviour is a simplified educational simulation.

components.name: Console stand
components.fastening: One 26.5 mm screw (coin or flathead), then lift the stand straight up. The spare screw and cap live in the stand's cubby.

info.what: The plastic foot that holds the console upright.
info.does: Keeps the console stable standing up. A screw in the foot's cubby lets it be locked on; lying flat it is a different stand.
info.ifFails: A missing stand lets a vertical console tip over.

onMissing.symptom: Stand removed: the console cannot stand upright.

components.name: Right faceplate
components.fastening: Clips only, no tools: lift a corner (USB and ethernet ports on the left), then slide it toward the bottom of the console.

info.what: The white curved side panel on the fan side.
info.does: Covers the fan grille and SSD cover and gives the console its look.
info.ifFails: A cracked plate is cosmetic, but dust gets in more easily.

onMissing.symptom: Right faceplate removed: the fan grille and SSD cover are exposed.

components.name: Fan grille
components.fastening: Pry up with a spudger in the gap above the fan, then lift it off.

info.what: The dust grille above the fan.
info.does: Lets air in while keeping large dust out.
info.ifFails: Clogged grille: loud fan and a hot console.

onMissing.symptom: Fan grille missing: dust gets straight into the fan.

components.name: SSD cover
components.fastening: One 17 mm Phillips (#0) screw, then slide the cover toward the top of the console to unclip it.

info.what: A small metal cover over the M.2 expansion bay.
info.does: Protects the expansion slot (and any SSD you add).
info.ifFails: Loose cover: nothing happens, the bay is just exposed.

onMissing.symptom: SSD cover missing: the expansion bay is exposed.

components.name: Fan shroud
components.fastening: Four TR9 Torx security screws (two 23.3 mm, one 11.4 mm, one 31 mm); lift the shroud straight up.

fasteners.notes: TR9 Torx security: 2 x 23.3 mm, 1 x 11.4 mm, 1 x 31 mm. The guide's tool list says TR8 but step 11 says TR9

info.what: A plastic duct around the fan.
info.does: Guides air from the fan across the heat sink.
info.ifFails: A loose shroud makes the fan louder and cools worse.

onMissing.symptom: Fan shroud missing: airflow is poorly guided.

components.name: Cooling fan

onDamaged.symptom: Fan is clogged or worn: very loud, the console runs hot and throttles.

components.fastening: Peel off the black wire cover (pry the cover only), pull the fan connector up from the motherboard, then lift the fan out.

fasteners.notes: Pry the wire cover, not the wires

info.what: A large 120 mm centrifugal ('squirrel cage') fan.
info.does: Pulls air through the console and over the heat sink so the chip stays cool.
info.ifFails: Dust or a worn bearing: loud fan, throttling and overheating shutdowns.
info.advanced: Under the black wire cover a connector links the fan to the motherboard. Pry only the cover, not the wires.

onMissing.symptom: Fan missing: the console overheats and shuts down within seconds.

components.name: Black inner shell (first half)
components.fastening: Peel the tamper-evident sticker over the last screw, remove eleven TR8 Torx security screws (six 18.6 mm, two 23.3 mm, two 43.2 mm, one 7.3 mm), then lift the shell straight up. The optical drive cable is disconnected first.

info.what: The black plastic shell under the white side panel.
info.does: Holds the drive, fan area and top shield in place.
info.ifFails: Cracks are rare; missing screws make the shell rattle.

onMissing.symptom: Inner shell missing: internals are exposed.

components.name: Blu-ray disc drive

onDamaged.symptom: Disc drive faulty: discs are not read or the tray grinds.

onIncompatible.symptom: Drive is paired to a different console: discs are not read.

components.fastening: Disconnect the drive's ribbon cable at the motherboard and at the drive (lock, then pull the blue tab); lift the drive out once the shell is off.

info.ifFails: Discs are not recognised, grinding, or the tray will not load.
info.advanced: iFixit's teardown reports the drive is paired to the motherboard, so a drive from another console will not read discs.

onMissing.symptom: No disc drive: discs cannot be read; digital games still work.

components.name: Top shield plate
components.fastening: Forty-two TR8 Torx security screws (forty-one 7.3 mm, one 43.2 mm). Antenna wires are tucked under stickers; peel and reseat them. Replacement thermal pads must match the original thickness.

fasteners.notes: TR8 Torx security: 41 x 7.3 mm, 1 x 43.2 mm

info.what: A metal plate over the main board.
info.does: Shields electronics from interference and presses thermal pads against the chips.
info.ifFails: A bent plate or lost screw can cause poor cooling or rattles.

onMissing.symptom: Top shield missing: the main board is exposed and cooling is poorer.

components.name: Left faceplate
components.fastening: Clips only: lift the corner with the PlayStation logo and slide it toward the bottom of the console.

info.what: The white side panel on the opposite side.
info.does: Covers the case and gives the console its look.

onMissing.symptom: Left faceplate removed: the inner shell is exposed.

components.name: Black inner shell (second half)
components.fastening: Two 29.4 mm TR8 Torx security screws hold it to the motherboard and heat sink assembly. Lift the front edge and push it back to clear the charging port.

info.what: The second half of the black plastic shell.
info.does: Closes the main board and power supply from the other side.

onMissing.symptom: Second shell half missing: the power supply and board are exposed.

components.name: Power supply (350 W)

onDamaged.symptom: Power supply failed: no power, or clicking and an instant shut-off.

onIncompatible.symptom: Power supply does not match this console: it will not power on.

components.fastening: Hold the rear shield plate down, grip the supply and lift it straight up to unplug it from the motherboard. Reach it only after the stand, both faceplates, grille, shroud, fan, SSD cover, optical drive, shells and top shield are off.

info.what: A 350 W enclosed power supply (Delta, ADP-400DR per iFixit's part listing).
info.does: Turns mains power into the voltages the console needs. Its power input prong slots into the supply.
info.ifFails: No power, clicking, or random shut-offs.
info.advanced: This slot is the engine's power source. 'Disconnect' stands for unplugging the mains cable and holding the power off before you touch electronics, which iFixit lists as step zero.

onMissing.symptom: Power supply missing: the console cannot power on.

components.name: Main board with heat sink

onDamaged.symptom: Main board fault: the console does not start.

components.fastening: Lift out after removing the remaining hardware and flipping it. The liquid metal on the processor must not be smeared.

info.what: The board with the custom AMD Zen 2 8-core CPU, RDNA 2 GPU, 16 GB GDDR6 and the 825 GB SSD, under a large heat sink.
info.does: Runs the console. Liquid metal between the chip and the heat sink moves heat out.
info.ifFails: No video, crashes, or overheating. Liquid metal is conductive and hard to replace.
info.advanced: iFixit lists the liquid metal as sealed in, and notes the Wi-Fi module and M.2 slot are on this board.

components.note: No iFixit removal guide for the board: the teardown only shows it. Screw count, order against the heat sink, and liquid-metal handling are not confirmed. Antenna, LED, power-button and USB board cables are not modelled as slots.

components.name: Chassis frame
components.fastening: The base everything mounts into. The USB, LED and power/eject button boards have their own iFixit guides and are not modelled separately.

info.what: The base frame the other parts mount to, with the front USB, LED and power/eject boards.
info.ifFails: Rarely fails; cracks or bent mounts.

components.note: Only the teardown shows it. Front boards and frame details are not confirmed per part.

spares.name: Clogged cooling fan
spares.condition: Blades and housing packed with dust, bearing rattles

effect.symptom: Fan is clogged: very loud, the console runs hot and throttles.

spares.name: Disc drive (re-paired)
spares.note: Healthy drive that has been paired to this console's motherboard.

spares.name: Disc drive from another console
spares.note: Fits physically but is paired to its original console.

spares.name: Failing disc drive
spares.condition: Tray grinds; discs are not recognised

spares.name: Failed power supply
spares.condition: Clicks and shuts off at once; swollen capacitors

cases.title: The Jet Engine
cases.brief: The PS5 sounds like a hair dryer and shuts down during long sessions. Dust has clogged the fan.
symptoms: The console runs hot and throttles.
cases.explanation: Dust packed the fan and slowed airflow, so the heat sink could not shed heat. iFixit's order is stand, faceplate, grille, shroud screws, wire cover, then the fan connector. Always unplug the console first. A fresh fan restored cooling.

cases.title: Disc Not Recognised
cases.brief: Games from the store work, but every disc is ejected or ignored. The drive grinds when you insert one.
cases.explanation: The disc drive failed. iFixit's teardown reports the drive is paired to its console's motherboard, so a drive from another console will not read discs even though it fits. You reach the drive by removing the fan and shell, and disconnecting its ribbon cable.

cases.title: Click, Then Silence
cases.brief: The console clicks once and shuts off whenever you press power. No lights stay on. The power supply is the suspect.
symptoms: No power; a click and an instant shut-off.
cases.explanation: A failed power supply cannot hold the voltages up, so the console trips off at once. iFixit rates the swap moderate: 41 steps, both faceplates, the shells, 42 top-shield screws and several antenna cables. The supply is lifted straight off the motherboard last. Keep every screw in its place.
